title: ECON 301 — Week 6: Heteroskedasticity
summary: This material covers heteroskedasticity in multiple linear regression models, explaining its consequences for OLS inference, robust standard errors (White), testing methods (Breusch–Pagan and White tests), and weighted least squares (WLS).

concepts.name: Homoskedasticity
concepts.summary: The assumption that the error variance conditional on the regressors is constant for every observation.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity
concepts.summary: A violation of the homoskedasticity assumption where the conditional variance of the error depends on the regressors.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard error
concepts.summary: Standard errors introduced by White (1980) that allow for valid statistical inference in the presence of unknown heteroskedasticity.

concepts.name: Breusch–Pagan test
concepts.summary: A statistical test for heteroskedasticity by regressing squared OLS residuals on the model regressors and checking joint significance.

concepts.name: White test
concepts.summary: A general test for heteroskedasticity that regresses squared residuals on regressors, their squares, and cross-products.

concepts.name: Weighted least squares
concepts.summary: An efficient estimation method used when the form of heteroskedasticity is known by weighting observations inversely to their error variance.
